lines.c1: A Kubernetes cluster has a control plane that makes decisions, and worker nodes that run your containers.
lines.c2: Every request goes through the API server. It is the front door, and the only component that talks to the database.
lines.c3: The desired state is stored in etcd, a consistent key-value store.
lines.c4: The scheduler watches for pods with no node, and picks a node for each one.
lines.c5: Controllers compare the desired state with reality, and act to close the gap.
lines.c6: On each node, the kubelet sees the pods assigned to it, and asks the container runtime to start them.
lines.c7: Each node also runs kube-proxy. It sets up network rules, so traffic sent to a Service reaches one of the right pods.
